3.1.intro: Your offer is what people get, and why they should buy now. We'll find its weakest part.

steps.say: Score your main product from 1 to 5 on each of these: **promise**, **belief**, **urgency**, **safety**, **easy yes**.
steps.check: You have five scores on one line.
steps.lost: Give each word a score from 1 to 5. Guess fast.

steps.say: Circle the lowest score. Open its lesson: promise 3.2, belief 3.3, urgency 3.4, safety 3.5, easy yes 3.6.
steps.check: You know the one thing to work on this week.
steps.lost: Circle the smallest number. That's your job this week.

3.2.intro: People buy when they can say what they'll get in one line. Your reviews already have the words.

steps.say: Read your 20 newest 4 and 5 star reviews. Copy the words people use for what they got.
steps.check: You have 5 to 10 phrases in customers' words.
steps.lost: Read five good reviews. Copy your favourite phrases.

steps.say: Write one sentence about the problem your product takes away. Use their words.
steps.check: You have one problem sentence, like "No more tangled cables in your bag".
steps.lost: Finish this: "No more ..."

steps.say: Write one sentence about how others will see your customer after they buy.
steps.check: You have a "how others see me" sentence.
steps.lost: Finish this: "People will think I'm ..."

steps.say:
Make one promise line.

1. Join your sentences into one line of 15 words or fewer.
2. In Shopify, open **Products** and pick the product.
3. Paste the line at the top of **Description**.
4. Use the same line to start your next ad.
steps.check: The same promise is on your product page and in an ad.
steps.careful: Say the result, not the feature. "Sleep through the night" beats "Memory foam core".
steps.lost: Write one short line about what people get. Put it at the top of your product page.

3.3.intro: People don't buy until they believe it will work for them. Let's answer their worries with proof.

steps.say: List 20 reasons someone might not buy. Look in support emails, reviews and return notes.
steps.check: You have a list of 20 worries.
steps.lost: Write five reasons people might not buy. Five is fine to start.

steps.say: Sort them into six groups: price, quality, fit or size, trust, timing, and "do I need it?".
steps.check: You can see which group is biggest.
steps.lost: Put each worry in a group. Which group has the most?

steps.say: Next to each worry, write one proof: a review, a photo, a guarantee, a fact or a demo video.
steps.check: Each worry has something you can show.
steps.lost: Pick one worry. Find one review or photo that answers it.

steps.say: Add the answers to your product page FAQ, your ads and your welcome emails. Start with the biggest group.
steps.check: Top worries are answered in at least three places.
steps.lost: Add one answer to your product page FAQ.

3.4.intro: If there's a real reason something might run out, people act sooner. It must be true.

steps.say: Pick one honest reason it might run out: a small batch, a preorder with a ship date, a short seasonal colour, or low stock.
steps.check: You picked one you can stand behind.
steps.lost: Pick one true reason it might run out.

steps.say: Write that reason in one sentence on the product page. For example: "Batch 4 of 6: 300 made, ships 14 November".
steps.check: Shoppers can see why it might go.
steps.lost: Write one honest sentence about why it might run out.

steps.say: Set up an email that goes out when stock drops below about 2 weeks of sales. Send it to people who looked at the product and to your best customers.
steps.check: The email sends by itself when stock is low.
steps.careful: Never use fake countdown timers or made-up stock numbers. In Australia, a court ordered a $15 million penalty after ACCC action, partly over a countdown timer that kept resetting.
steps.lost: Set up a low-stock email in your email app. You can do it later too.

3.5.intro: Shoppers worry about buying the wrong thing. Each worry you remove means more orders.

steps.say: Turn on photo reviews in your review app. Email recent buyers and ask for a photo with their review.
steps.check: Your best sellers show reviews with photos.
steps.lost: Ask three happy customers for a photo review.

steps.say: Add a size chart to every product where fit matters.
steps.check: A size guide link sits above **Add to cart**.
steps.lost: Add a size chart to your best seller. No sizes? Skip this card.

steps.say: Turn on live chat for your opening hours. Shopify Inbox is free.
steps.check: A chat bubble shows on your store, and messages reach your phone.
steps.lost: Install Shopify Inbox. Turn it on.

steps.say: Add a real face: a photo of you and two sentences on your About page.
steps.check: Shoppers can see a real person.
steps.lost: Add one photo of you to your About page.

steps.say: Write a shipping promise you can keep, like "Ships within 24 hours, Monday to Friday". Add a clear returns policy. Show both near the price.
steps.check: On a phone, you see shipping time and returns without scrolling.
steps.careful: After changing returns, watch your return rate for 60 days to check it's worth it.
steps.lost: Write one line: when it ships. Put it near the price.

3.6.intro: How a price looks changes how it feels. Try one small idea at a time.

steps.say: Add a cost-per-use line under the price. For example "Under $1 a day" for a $29 monthly product.
steps.check: The price feels smaller, but it's the same.
steps.lost: Divide the price by days used. Write that under the price.

steps.say: Try one higher price on one product for two weeks, for example $39 to $49.
steps.check: You can compare sales and profit. Sometimes sales barely change and you keep more.
steps.lost: Raise one price. Check again in two weeks.

steps.say: Show a bigger option, or the full bundle value, next to the single price.
steps.check: The single price looks like better value.
steps.lost: Put a bigger option next to your normal one.

steps.say: Add a middle option that makes your favourite option look like the obvious pick.
steps.check: More shoppers choose your favourite option.
steps.lost: Add a middle option. Watch what people pick.

steps.say: Test free shipping against a lower price. Then turn on a pay-in-parts option in **Settings > Payments** for pricier items. Shop Pay Installments is only for US, Canadian and UK stores.
steps.check: You know what customers like better, and they can pay in parts.
steps.lost: Turn on pay-in-parts in **Settings > Payments**.

3.7.intro: Not every product deserves your ad money. A quick monthly check shows which ones do.

steps.say: For each product, write last month's ad spend, sales, return (sales ÷ ad spend), units sold and margin.
steps.check: One row per product, five numbers each.
steps.lost: Start with your top 3 products. Five numbers each.

steps.say: Put each product in one of the four boxes in the lesson table. Do the action for that box.
steps.check: Every product has a box and a next step.
steps.lost: Is each product's return good or bad? Is spend high or low? That picks its box.

steps.say: In your next weekly check, move ad money towards the "good return" products.
steps.check: More of your spend goes to products that pay it back.
steps.lost: Give a bit more ad money to your best-return product.

3.8.intro: New products help you grow. Test them cheaply first so you don't lock up cash.

steps.say: Start an ideas list: customer requests, reviews, search terms, and things that go with your best sellers.
steps.check: You have at least 5 ideas, each with a reason.
steps.lost: Write three product ideas and why.

steps.say: Test your best idea cheaply: a waitlist page, a preorder, a small batch, or asking 5 creators.
steps.check: You have real proof people want it, like sign-ups or preorders.
steps.lost: Make a simple waitlist page for one idea.

steps.say: Plan the launch (Lessons 13.2 and 13.3): build excitement, early access, a launch offer, and ads ready.
steps.check: The launch has dates, an offer and ads before day one.
steps.lost: Write a launch date and one launch offer.

steps.say: After 30 days, check the new product with the snapshot from Lesson 3.7.
steps.check: It's in one of the four boxes, with a next step.
steps.lost: Set a reminder for 30 days after launch.

3.9.intro: Offers get old. Others copy them. A regular check keeps yours fresh.

steps.say: Add a calendar reminder every 3 months: review my offer.
steps.check: The next review date is in your calendar.
steps.lost: Add one calendar reminder for 3 months from today.

steps.say: If sales from visitors drop for 2 weeks and you can't find why, redo the five scores from Lesson 3.1.
steps.check: You have fresh scores and one change to try.
steps.lost: Sales slow for 2 weeks? Go back to Lesson 3.1.

3.10.intro: If people use your product up, a subscription can turn one sale into many. It only suits things people reorder.

steps.say: Look at customers who bought twice. How many days between their orders, usually?
steps.check: You know your reorder gap, like 30 or 60 days, or that repeats are too rare.
steps.lost: Find two repeat customers. Count the days between orders.

steps.say: Install a subscription app from the Shopify App Store. Offer one simple plan: a small saving (5% to 15%) or free shipping, every reorder gap, with easy skip and cancel.
steps.check: The product page shows "One-time purchase" and "Subscribe and save".
steps.lost: Install a subscription app. Make one simple plan.

steps.say: Send an email offering the subscription a few days before the first order likely runs out.
steps.check: New buyers get the offer right when they'd reorder.
steps.lost: Add one subscription email after purchase.

steps.say: Each month, check subscribers, cancels and the reasons. Fix the top reason.
steps.check: You know how many subscribers you have and why people leave.
steps.careful: Make cancelling and skipping easy. Hiding it causes chargebacks and angry reviews.
steps.lost: Once a month, read why people cancelled. Fix the most common one.
